record.title: Architecture Overview
record.body:
This page describes the runtime architecture behind Harmony Games' live mobile titles - Domino Delights (internal codename Game of Dominoes / GoD) and Zombie Match 3D (listed as Puzzles vs Zombies until July 2025) - plus the shared platform that Combo Fighter and future titles ride on. It is the canonical starting point for new engineers; deep-dives live on the linked pages.

This runs across several AWS accounts organised under Control Tower. The split is mixed rather than uniform: Domino Delights has separate dev and prod accounts, Zombie Match 3D runs both environments out of a single account, and the analytics pipeline has its own account serving QA and production alike. Infra is defined in AWS CDK (v2, TypeScript) - there is no click-ops. If it's not in the CDK app, it doesn't exist. See the AWS Infrastructure Guide for the account layout and deploy flow.

Client tier

Both live games ship a single Unity codebase built for iOS and Android. The Unity client is a fairly thin presentation layer: it renders the board, handles input and local animation, and caches recent state so a cold start feels instant. Authoritative game logic - economy, matchmaking, progression, anti-cheat validation - lives server-side. Clients talk to the backend over HTTPS/JSON and hold a short-lived session token issued at login.

  • Store builds are cut on a self-hosted Jenkins farm and shipped via TestFlight (AppCenter was used until March 2025); release tagging is manual per title.
  • Attribution and install tracking go through Singular; there is no second attribution SDK in the client.
  • Telemetry is emitted from the client and does not hit the backend directly - see the analytics section below.

Backend services

Zombie Match 3D's backend is written in Elixir/Phoenix; Domino Delights runs a separate Node.js/Express service and Combo Fighter its own Node/CDK stack. The Elixir services run as containers on AWS ECS Fargate each behind its own public Application Load Balancer on its own hostname. Each service is its own task definition and target group; only the Nakama ALB does host-header routing, and only to split the admin console off the client API. State is persisted in Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2 (a single serverless writer per cluster; see match3d-backend/zombies-game-cdk/lib/constructs/database.ts). We lean on Elixir's supervision trees and BEAM concurrency so a crashing session process never takes down the node. Details and the service catalog live on Backend Services - Elixir/Phoenix.

Social & multiplayer

The social and real-time multiplayer layer is Nakama, run as its own Fargate service per title. Zombie Match 3D's Nakama uses a nakama database on the shared Aurora cluster; Domino Delights' Nakama runs against its own standalone RDS PostgreSQL instance. Nakama owns teams, team chat, team leaderboards and storage. There is no match runtime or matchmaking in it - head-to-head modes are not served by Nakama, and Combo Fighter does not use it at all. Our Phoenix services are wired to call Nakama over its internal API rather than reimplementing sessions or presence - though on Zombie Match 3D that server-to-server path is switched off in production, so team-leaderboard progress is not pushed from the backend there. Operational runbooks are on Nakama Server Setup & Operations.

Component summary

ComponentTechRuns onNotes
Game clientUnity (C#)iOS / AndroidThin client; one codebase per title
Game backendElixir / Phoenix (ZM3D); Node.js (DD, CF)ECS Fargate + ALBAuthoritative economy & progression
Social / multiplayerNakamaECS FargateTeams, team chat, team leaderboards, team lives bank
Primary datastoreAurora PostgreSQLAurora Serverless v2Shared cluster; schema per service group
Infra as codeAWS CDK v2CISeveral accounts under Control Tower; the dev/prod split differs per title

Telemetry & analytics

Gameplay and monetization events flow from the Unity client into Firebase, and are exported natively into BigQuery, where dbt models them for the Metabase boards. Server-side events take a separate AWS path (API Gateway -> Kinesis -> Firehose -> S3, catalogued by AWS Glue for Athena). The backend is deliberately out of this path so a telemetry spike never adds load to the game services. The full pipeline, schemas, and dashboards are documented on Analytics Integration - Unity → Snowflake.

Keep this page conceptual. Do not paste account IDs, ALB DNS names, connection strings, or bundle IDs here - those belong in the AWS Infrastructure Guide and the secrets manager, not the wiki.

record.title: AWS Infrastructure Guide
record.body:
This page documents how Harmony Games runs its backend on AWS. It complements the Architecture Overview (the big picture) and the Nakama Server Setup & Operations runbook (the game-server specifics). If you are new to the infra, read the Architecture Overview first, then come back here for the AWS-level detail.

We are a ten-person studio at this revision - seven paid staff plus three unpaid founders - down from a 2024 peak of 19 after the October 2025 reduction - so the guiding principle is managed over self-hosted. Almost everything below is a managed AWS service so we don't run a platform team. We bootstrapped the first two years largely on AWS Activate credits before we were paying list price.

Account & region layout

Accounts are split under Control Tower by title and by environment, and inconsistently: Domino Delights has separate dev and prod accounts, Zombie Match 3D uses one account for both (separated only by region), and the analytics pipeline has its own account shared by QA and prod. Region assignment is per component rather than one primary: the Zombie Match 3D backend is us-west-2 in prod and us-east-2 in dev, the Domino Delights backend is us-east-2 in prod, and the analytics pipeline runs in us-east-2. us-east-2 is a live environment, not a DR footprint. Everything sits inside a multi-AZ VPC (three availability zones), with public subnets for the load balancer and private subnets for compute and data.

Services in use

LayerAWS serviceWhat it does for us
ComputeECS FargateRuns the containerized Phoenix API and the Nakama game server. No EC2 hosts to patch.
DatabaseAurora PostgreSQLPrimary transactional store for player state, economy and live-ops config. Aurora Serverless v2, single writer, no read replicas. Non-standard port 5433.
IngressApplication Load BalancerEach stack has its own public ALB on its own hostname - Phoenix, Nakama and the Domino Delights Node service are not behind a shared load balancer.
CertificatesACMTLS certs for each title's own game domain, auto-renewed and attached to each ALB. harmonygames.co is the marketing site only.
Event lakeS3Raw client and server events land here as the analytics data lake.
Streaming / ETLKinesis + GlueKinesis ingests the event firehose; Glue jobs transform and partition it in S3, where a Glue crawler catalogues the processed prefix so Athena can query it in place. The reporting layer itself is BigQuery + Metabase; the Snowflake replica is a separate hand-refreshed copy (see the analytics integration page).
ObservabilityCloudWatch + X-RayContainer logs, alarms and dashboards (CloudWatch) plus X-Ray traces on the identity-component Lambdas, the quests Lambdas, the analytics-pipeline Lambdas and the Domino Delights Node service (X-Ray daemon sidecar). The Elixir/Phoenix backend and Nakama are not traced.

Analytics pipeline

The event path is worth calling out because it spans two regions. Clients and the game server emit events; those are written into Kinesis streams, dropped to S3 in raw form, and then Glue crawls and ETLs them into the curated tables our warehouse reads. This is the AWS half of the flow; the warehouse side lives on the analytics team's docs.

  • us-west-2 - game backend and Aurora. (Analytics ingestion is NOT here: the analytics CDK stack is single-region us-east-2 for both QA and prod.)
  • us-east-2 - Glue jobs, curated S3, cross-region backup copies.

Deploys

Service images are built locally by cdk deploy and pushed to ECR from a developer machine, then rolled out to the relevant Fargate service with a rolling update behind the ALB health checks. CI runs lint and tests only - it does not deploy any service. The one CI-driven deploy in the org is the marketing site's S3 sync (website/.github/workflows/s3-deploy*.yml). There is no manual SSH step - a failed health check rolls the task back automatically.

Cost note (estimates only). These are rough monthly figures pulled from Cost Explorer for planning; treat them as directional, not billing-accurate.

  • Fargate (Phoenix + Nakama): ~$650/mo
  • Aurora Serverless v2 (single writer): ~$420/mo
  • S3 + Kinesis + Glue (analytics): ~$300/mo
  • ALB + data transfer + CloudWatch/X-Ray: ~$180/mo

The single biggest lever is right-sizing Fargate task memory - check the CloudWatch utilization dashboard before bumping a task definition.

Ownership

Infra was owned by Douglas (Engineering, departed Oct 2025); with the team wound down, changes now go through the remaining executive owner. If you need a new IAM role, a subnet change, or a new Glue job, open an ENG ticket and tag it infra - do not click around in the console for anything that touches production networking.

Service inventory

There is no single production account and no single primary region: every CDK stack takes account and region from CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT / CDK_DEFAULT_REGION at deploy time, and the npm deploy scripts set them per title and per environment (see the account & region layout above). Compute is containerised on ECS Fargate; state is Aurora PostgreSQL; the analytics path is Kinesis → Glue → S3.

ServiceAWS primitiveNotes
Game APIECS FargateElixir/Phoenix; autoscaled on CPU utilization (target 80%, 3-10 tasks) behind an ALB
Social / accountsECS Fargate (Nakama)client API 7350 / HTTP admin 7351 behind an HTTPS ALB; 7349 is exposed in local dev only
Primary datastoreAurora PostgreSQLAurora Serverless v2, single writer, no read replicas; automated snapshots
Event streamKinesis Data StreamsClient telemetry ingestion; feeds Glue
ETLAWS GlueBatches Kinesis records to partitioned Parquet in S3
LakeS3Partitioned by event date; the BI warehouse loads from here

Scaling & limits

Fargate services scale horizontally; Aurora Serverless v2 scales capacity units with load; there is no reader endpoint. Concurrency was never instrumented: the ~1K figure in the Google Drive sheet “Domino Delights _ Beta Launch Readiness_” (tab Beta Checklist, row 26) was a peak-CCU launch target, not a measurement, and it is CCU rather than DAU. Peak measured DAU was ~1,240 (Domino Delights, late June 2025). Cost, not capacity, has been the constraint.

Cost control: non-prod runs at reduced capacity rather than zero (a dev Fargate floor of 1-2 tasks and an Aurora Serverless v2 minimum of 0.5 ACU); the Kinesis stream is provisioned with a single shard. The AWS activation credits materially offset the first year of spend.

Deploy & rollback

Infrastructure is AWS CDK; application deploys are rolling on Fargate with health-check gating. Rollback is redeploy of the previous task-definition revision.

Disaster recovery

Aurora automated backups + manual pre-release snapshots; S3 is versioned and the lake is reproducible from Kinesis replay within the retention window. RPO is the snapshot cadence; RTO is dominated by Aurora restore time.

FailureMitigationRecovery
Writer AZ lossAurora Serverless v2, single writer - no standby instanceAWS restarts the writer in a healthy AZ from the shared cluster volume; expect minutes of downtime, not a sub-minute failover. (Domino Delights' Nakama RDS instance is separately multi-AZ and does fail over.)
Bad migrationPre-release snapshotRestore snapshot; replay Kinesis
Accidental S3 deleteBucket versioningRestore prior version

On-call

Alarms page the two-person rota via the on-call tool. The first responder triages; anything touching Aurora or a data migration escalates to Arthur Blake before any write action.

record.title: Nakama Server Setup & Operations
record.body:
This page covers how we run Nakama (the open-source game server) for Harmony Games' live titles - deploy, admin console access, and database migration ops. Nakama backs social features (teams, team chat, team leaderboards, storage). There is a separate deployment per title - one per title, each on that title's own social hostname - not one shared social layer. Nakama itself is LIVE in Zombie Match 3D production - client API on prod-social.zombies-game.com, admin console on prod-social-admin.zombies-game.com, up since 31 July 2025. What is disabled there is the Phoenix backend's server-to-server call into Nakama, so level-completion progress is never pushed to the team-leaderboard RPC in prod; client traffic - teams, chat, lives bank, leaderboard reads - is unaffected (NAKAMA_ENABLED=false). For the wider picture see Architecture Overview, and for VPC / cluster details see AWS Infrastructure Guide.

Runtime topology

Nakama ships as a single Docker image and runs on ECS Fargate behind an HTTPS Application Load Balancer. Zombie Match 3D's Nakama uses that title's shared Aurora PostgreSQL cluster for state; Domino Delights' Nakama runs against its own dedicated RDS PostgreSQL instance. Which one applies depends on the title - this page's own intro already notes there is a separate deployment per title. The ALB terminates TLS on a single HTTPS listener and forwards to the container on the client API port 7350, with the HTTP admin and metrics port 7351 routed by host header. The gRPC port 7349 is exposed in local dev only and is not mapped in AWS. If a task keeps getting OOM-killed, bump memory before touching CPU - Nakama is memory-bound long before it is CPU-bound at our concurrency.

Deploy

Deploys are a rolling ECS service update: push the tagged image to ECR, then update the service to the new task definition revision. The ALB drains connections on the old task before it stops. Roll back by pointing the service at the previous task definition revision - do not delete old revisions.

bash

Admin console & DB migrations

Admin console

The Nakama admin console is served on port 7351 and is currently exposed on the public ALB at the per-title social-admin hostname - there is no VPC restriction and no VPN in front of it. Console credentials are set in config/production.yml in the repo rather than Secrets Manager, which is a known gap. Treat the console as read-mostly in prod - use it to inspect accounts, storage objects, and leaderboard state, not to hand-edit live data.

Database migrations

Nakama runs against its own logical database (nakama) on the Aurora cluster, separate from the Phoenix app's zombies_game_prod, and applies migrations on boot. Migration notes for operators:

  • Migrations run automatically when a new image starts; a failed migration fails the health check, so the bad task never takes traffic.
  • Before a version bump that includes a schema change, snapshot the Aurora cluster.
  • Never run two different Nakama image versions against the same database at once - keep the rolling deploy to a single version transition.

Nakama migrations are forward-only. There is no automatic down-migration - recovery from a bad schema change is restore-from-snapshot, so take the snapshot first. All server logs go to CloudWatch with a 1-month retention window; pull the failing task's log stream there when a deploy stalls in PROVISIONING.

- Douglas, Platform/Backend

record.title: Analytics Integration — Unity → Snowflake
record.body:
This page separates the retained analytics systems rather than treating them as one warehouse path.

Pipeline overview

  1. Product/client analytics: Unity emits Firebase telemetry; Firebase's native export writes title-specific BigQuery marts, and Metabase surfaces the product boards.
  2. Server-event telemetry: API Gateway feeds Kinesis and Firehose, which write S3; Glue catalogues and processes the lake for Athena.
  3. Attribution: Singular provides install and paid-acquisition attribution.

Event categories

Every event carries a common envelope (app version, platform, device class, session id, server timestamp). At a high level events fall into five categories:

CategoryFires onUsed for
SessionApp open / close, foreground / backgroundDAU, session length, retention curves
ProgressionLevel start / complete / failDifficulty tuning, funnel drop-off
Resource / economyCurrency and life grant / spendSink-source balance, economy health
Ad impressionRewarded / interstitial shown & completedAd revenue, fill rate, eCPM
Client errorHandled exceptions, load stallsCrash triage, release health

Adding or changing an event

  • Register the event name and payload in that title's AnalyticsManager before shipping - do not free-type event names in game code.
  • New fields must be nullable; the Glue transform tolerates extra keys but will not backfill missing ones.
  • Flag any type change (int → string, etc.) to eng before release - it breaks the replica's COPY column mapping.

record.title: Quest System — Design & Incident Postmortem
record.body:
Owner: Arthur Blake (Engineering) · Space: ENG · Related ticket: ENG-1892

Live quest configuration is player-facing on both iOS and Android. Never push quest changes straight to the live quest server. QA sign-off and a canary are now mandatory - see the Lessons & Follow-ups section below.

Design: How the Quest System Works

The quest system drives the daily engagement loop on both Domino Delights and Zombie Match 3D - one shared API Gateway service with Node Lambdas and 8 DynamoDB tables, whose prod URL is hardcoded in both clients (internal codename GoD). A single quest-config service owns the catalog of quest templates; clients pull the active set on session start and render the daily quest tray.

Quest lifecycle

  • Population - at the daily boundary the quest server selects a template set and materializes concrete quest instances (target, reward, progress counters) per player segment.
  • Reset - the previous day's quests are cleared and a fresh set is populated. Reset fires on a single global EventBridge cron - daily, plus weekly on Monday - in UTC. There is no per-player local-midnight logic.
  • Progression - gameplay events (levels cleared, boosters used, ad views) increment the matching quest counters; completion grants the reward.

Quest types

TypeTriggerTypical reward
PlayLevels cleared in a sessionCoins
BoosterBoosters usedBoosters
AdsRewarded-ad views completedCoins / lives

Quest templates are shared with the Live-Ops Event Engine so seasonal events can layer bonus quests on top of the daily set.

Incident Postmortem - Daily Quests Not Populating (ENG-1892)

On November 15, 2024 the quest list stopped populating entirely on both iOS and Android — the daily and weekly tabs both came back empty. The first report was 15:51 UTC, when the client began failing to retrieve quests; ENG-1892 was opened at 17:42 UTC. Pulling the offending template from the design sheet that evening did not clear it - a broader quest fix was merged the next morning, and the incident was not resolved until 18 November at 17:44 UTC. The outage ran from the first report at 15:51 on 15 November to 17:44 on 18 November — 73h53m of player-facing downtime. The ticket's own open-to-Done span is shorter, 72h02m, because ENG-1892 was not raised until 17:42, nearly two hours after players were first affected. Cause: an Ads-subtype row added to a live quest design sheet, which the 8-hourly ingestor pushed straight to the production quests table — shipped clients could not deserialize it, so the whole response failed. There was no dev/prod separation between quest sheets.

Timeline

Time (UTC)Event
2024-11-15 15:51First report: retrieving quests fails on the client; daily and weekly trays both come back empty on iOS and Android.
2024-11-15 17:42ENG-1892 opened - “The quests are not populated at all in both platforms”.
2024-11-15 18:20Confirmed reset also failing; scoped to the quest-config service, not the clients.
2024-11-15 19:30Offending Ads-type quest removed from the daily-quest sheet.
2024-11-16Removing the row alone had not cleared it; a broader quest fix was merged. No root-cause note was written back to ENG-1892.
2024-11-18 16:30Quest server redeploy rolled out. The Google-Sheets ingestor's 8-hour auto-deploy was not changed.
2024-11-18 17:44Quests re-populated and reset normally; ENG-1892 closed. Incident resolved.

Root cause

Established during the incident but never written back to the ticket - ENG-1892 carries no root-cause note. An Ads-subtype quest row reached the live catalog through an unreviewed auto-deploy path for quest config: an EventBridge rule fires the ingestor Lambda every 8 hours, which reads the design Google Sheet and rewrites the live quests, chests and achievements DynamoDB tables wholesale - it deletes every existing row and re-PUTs the sheet's contents. Whatever the trigger, the population and reset routine failed for the whole catalog, so the daily set was never materialized - hence empty trays and no reset.

Because population is all-or-nothing per run, a single bad template takes down every quest for every player. There is no per-template isolation today.

Fix

  • Removed the offending Ads-type quest template from the catalog.
  • The ingestor's 8-hour auto-deploy was left running: neither its cadence nor the Google Sheet it reads was changed, so a template only stays removed if it is removed from the sheet.
  • Redeployed; quests re-populated and reset resumed.

Lessons & Follow-ups

  • Quest config changes need QA sign-off before they reach the live catalog.
  • Add a canary: stage new quest templates to a small segment and verify population/reset before full rollout.
  • Fold quest pushes into the Release Checklist & Store Submission so nothing ships unreviewed.

record.title: Live-Ops Event Engine
record.body:
The Live-Ops Event Engine powers all recurring in-game events for Zombie Match 3D (listed as "Puzzles vs Zombies" until the July 2025 store rename). It defines, schedules, and fires timed content - Plague Race, Zombie Lane, Endless Monster Mode - and drives the associated leaderboards and lives economy. This page documents the architecture, the scheduler's known fragility, and the July 2025 outage that took Domino Delights live events dark - the record never marks it restored. For upcoming cadence and slot ownership see Live-Ops Event Calendar & Planning.

Architecture

The engine has three cooperating parts. Event definitions are reward tables authored by design in Google Sheets and hot-loaded by the backend; the scheduler is the runtime that evaluates windows and fires state transitions; the leaderboard service ranks entries and settles rewards at event close.

ComponentResponsibilityOwner
Event definitionsReward tables are authored in Google Sheets and imported hourly; windows are cron expressions baked into the CDK stack; there is no remote kill-switch for live events - Domino Delights gates them on a compiled client constant and Zombie Match 3D's per-event flags are literals in the backend runtime config, so turning an event on or off means a deploy or a direct database edit. There is no cohort-targeting field.Design (Julia Lawson)
SchedulerEach event type runs its own cron, all at 00:00 UTC - Plague Race, Endless Monster daily and Boss Arena daily; Leagues, Endless Monster weekly and Collect & Win weekly; Season Pass monthly on the 1st at 00:00 UTC (the CDK sets its schedule to 0 0 1 * * in production and the module is the monthly season-pass server); each season then runs to the start of the next month, which is the monthly window the Season Pass spec describes). The Quantum scheduler runs both: the four Google-Sheets reward importers (hourly in production) and every event-reset job - each leaderboard server registers its own Quantum job at boot from the cron string on its leaderboard row, so event firing and reward import share one scheduler. Lives regeneration is not on any of these.Backend (Douglas)
Leaderboard serviceIngests scores during a window, freezes and settles rewards at closeBackend

Lives regeneration

Life regeneration is computed client-side from server time and written back to the server; the server only clamps negative values. It is not on the scheduler and shares no failure domain with event firing - the two are independent. The July 2025 outage saw both symptoms at once, but that was co-occurrence: the stuck-lives reports are a separate, still-open client-side bug (ENG-2277, ENG-2400). See the incident below.

Scheduler has no leader: every node runs its own. The scheduler is a supervised in-process Quantum instance on EVERY node, not a cluster-wide singleton: jobs register with a node-local run strategy while production runs three Fargate tasks, so each event-reset cron currently fires once per task. A crashed process is restarted in place by its own supervisor; what it does not survive is a deploy that leaves the job unscheduled. A single stalled process does not stop event firing; what does is a deploy that leaves the job unscheduled on every node, which is how the July 2025 stall happened. Lives are unaffected - they are computed on the client. Do not add new subsystems to the tick loop without a leader-election plan.

July 2025 outage

From at least Jul 11, 2025 the event scheduler stopped advancing for Domino Delights, and no message anywhere in the record marks it restored. The same failure had happened a fortnight earlier and was cleared by hand. Lives are computed client-side (see above) and are not on the scheduler, so the stall could not stop the timer. The stuck-lives reports in the same thread are a separate, still-open bug (ENG-2277, ENG-2400) whose cause was never established. The lives write path stayed up throughout - backend granted manual lives top-ups on 14, 19 and 24 July while events were still not firing - and other accounts regenerated normally on the same build. The earliest symptom in the July thread is missing weekend events, reported on Jul 12, 2025 alongside a lives timer stuck at four. The 03:41 on Jul 13 figure is one reported player's lives balance beginning to fall in Metabase, not a first observation - a ticket relayed on Jul 12 said the problem had already been running for three days. Players reported seeing only two live events on the weekend, with River Rush, Streak Fever and Axe Arena not firing. It was not global - other accounts regenerated lives normally throughout - and no end date exists in the record: the same player's lives were broken again on Jul 24, coin balances were reported stuck negative on Jul 28, the same events-not-firing-until-someone-triggers-the-scheduler-by-hand failure was still being reported on Oct 27, and a lives-regeneration bug (ENG-2400) opened on Nov 2, 2025 was never closed. Zombie Match 3D was unaffected; its Plague Race ran normally that week. No standalone ticket was cut at the time; the timeline was reconstructed afterwards from support threads and scheduler logs.

Measure this outage from LIVE_EVENT_PERFORMANCE status and participation on Domino Delights, not from a revenue delta. Domino Delights revenue declined steadily across Jun-Jul 2025 as part of that title's wind-down, before, during and after the window; do not read that trend as outage impact.

Remediation

  • Add a heartbeat + external watchdog that pages on a missed scheduler tick (target: alert within 5 minutes, not 12+ hours).
  • Monitor the lives write-back route independently of scheduler ticks, so two co-occurring symptoms in different failure domains can be told apart on the first day rather than the third.
  • Introduce leader election so each cron fires once cluster-wide instead of once per Fargate task (Quantum.RunStrategy.Global, or an external lock).
  • Build a repro harness for ENG-2277 / ENG-2400 - every reported case was cleared only by a manual backend lives grant, and no fix was ever shipped.
  • Dashboard the scheduler's last-tick timestamp alongside revenue so drift is visible on the same screen.

Design context for the lives and event-timing models and the related quest timing regression lives in Quest System - Design & Incident Postmortem.

record.title: QA Regression Runbook
record.body:
Manual QA regression pass run against every release candidate before we submit a build for review. Last owned by QA (Arthur Blake, who took it over from Vincent Parker when Vincent Parker left in Nov 2025; Arthur Blake stayed through the February 2026 wind-down); anyone cutting a build can run it, but a green matrix here is a gate on the Release Checklist & Store Submission. Scope covers Domino Delights (internal codename GoD, "Game of Dominoes"), Zombie Match 3D (listed as "Puzzles vs Zombies" until the July 2025 rename) and Combo Fighter. Budget a few hours per title - the first five chapters alone run over an hour; if something fails, file the bug and block the release, don't hand-wave it.

Test the UPDATE path, not just a fresh install. The June 2025 progression losses were on Domino Delights, and nobody ever reproduced them - the leading hypothesis was the update path, which is why we test it. Every candidate must be installed over the last two shipped versions and checked for save/progression loss before we ship. If we only test fresh installs we will miss this entire class of bug again.

Recurring bug classes to always check

These four have all bitten us in production. Treat them as non-negotiable checks on every pass, on real devices, not just the emulator.

  • Font / asset download stall on splash. In May 2025 Domino Delights froze at roughly 22% on the splash screen while pulling remote fonts and assets (ENG-2346, build 0.2.197). Watch the loading bar all the way to gameplay; test on a throttled/slow connection and with the app cache cleared.
  • Lives & scheduler regeneration. Confirm lives tick back up on the timer, refill correctly after device clock changes, and that offline time is credited without over-granting.
  • Quest population & reset. New quests populate on a fresh session, complete correctly, and roll over at the daily/weekly reset without duplicating or leaving empty slots.
  • Save / progression integrity. Level, coins and unlocks survive an update, a force-quit and a re-launch. This is the one the June 2025 wipe belongs to.

Regression matrix

Run each row on at least one iOS and one Android device. Both update rows are mandatory - N-1 and N-2 are the last two shipped store versions.

AreaFresh installUpdate from N-1Update from N-2Notes
Splash / asset loadPassPassPassWatch for the ~22% stall (May 2025 Domino Delights)
Save / progressionPassPassPassJune 2025 wipe never reproduced in-house; update path is the leading hypothesis
Lives & schedulerPassPassPassTest with device clock changes
Quests populate / resetPassPassPassCheck daily + weekly rollover
Purchase / restorePassPassPassSandbox account. NOTE: entitlements do not restore on reinstall and receipts are not validated server-side - see the per-title IAP row below. Check the purchase grants client-side, not that it restores.

If a check fails

  • File the bug with device, OS version, source build and repro steps, and link it here.
  • A failure in any UPDATE column blocks the release - fresh-install-only regressions do not pass the gate.
  • Player-facing symptoms (lost progress, stuck splash, missing lives) should be mirrored to the Customer Support Playbook so support has a known-issue note before it hits the store.

Once the matrix is green, tick the QA sign-off on the Release Checklist & Store Submission before submitting to the stores.

Per-title regression matrix

Each release candidate is walked through the full matrix below on at least one iOS and one Android device. A cell fails the gate if the observed behaviour deviates from the expected column; file the bug, mark the matrix red, and block the submission.

record.title: Backend Services — Elixir/Phoenix
record.body:
This page describes the Elixir/Phoenix backend service, which sits behind Zombie Match 3D (listed as "Puzzles vs Zombies" until July 2025). Domino Delights ("Game of Dominoes"/GoD internally) runs a separate Node.js/Express service, and Combo Fighter its own Node/CDK stack - see "Runtime topology" below. The services own authoritative game state, player profiles, quests, and live-ops delivery. For the wider system picture and how these tie into Unity and Nakama, see Architecture Overview; teams, team chat and team leaderboards are documented separately in Nakama Server Setup & Operations.

Ownership is deliberately thin - a ten-person studio at this revision - seven paid staff plus three unpaid founders (down from a 2024 peak of 19 after the October 2025 reduction) can't staff a service mesh. Each title owns its own backend - all three were forked from the same AWS game-backend sample and allowed to diverge. Zombie Match 3D runs this Elixir/Phoenix app on Aurora; Domino Delights runs a separate Node.js/Express service on DynamoDB; Combo Fighter has its own Node/CDK stack, though its client also calls this Phoenix API. Prefer boring and observable over clever.

Runtime & deployment

This app is a single ordinary Mix project (:zombies_game), not an umbrella, released with mix release into one container image and run as one ECS Fargate service. Live-ops schedules run in-process on a Quantum cron inside that service; quests and identity are separate serverless stacks (see the table below)

  • Compute: ECS Fargate, one task definition per service, each behind its own public ALB (the Phoenix game API on prod-backend.zombies-game.com).
  • Data: Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2 (a single serverless writer, no read replica), Ecto for access, migrations gated in CI.
  • Infra as code: everything provisioned via AWS CDK - VPC, clusters, task definitions, and Aurora are all defined in the CDK app so environments (dev/prod) stay in lockstep.

Auth

Auth is split, and the two halves are documented on different pages. Nakama owns accounts, friends and sessions (see Nakama Setup and the API reference); this Phoenix service does not issue tokens of its own - it verifies JWTs issued by our own identity service via a Joken JWKS strategy (aws_auth/verifier.ex; issuer read from the ISSUER_ENDPOINT environment variable in config/runtime.exs, JWKS at $ISSUER_ENDPOINT/.well-known/jwks.json, audience gamebackend). There is no third-party identity broker. The issuer is the AWS Game Backend Framework Custom Identity Component, deployed from our own CDK app (match3d-backend-auth): Python Lambdas behind API Gateway over DynamoDB, publishing an RS256 key set through CloudFront and rotating it weekly. Its CDK records the reason Cognito is not used - a cdk-nag suppression reading "The API cannot use Cognito User Pools as it is an API built for login and authentication for custom identities." The @moduledoc on verifier.ex still says "AWS Cognito JWT Joken strategy"; that string is inherited from the AWS sample and is stale. Short-lived JWTs are validated on login; every other service validates the JWT signature locally (no per-request network hop) and trusts the sub claim as the player ID. Device-bound refresh tokens are stored in the identity service's own schema. Live-ops and quest mutations additionally require an internal service token - never a player JWT.

Services

identityLogin, JWT issuance/rotation, device binding; federates Sign in with Apple on iOS and Google Play Games on Android, layered over anonymous guest identitiesPython Lambdas behind API Gateway (separate stack)DynamoDB
game_stateAuthoritative match/board state, progression, save reconciliationthis Phoenix serviceAurora
profilePlayer profile, inventory, wallet (coins/lives)this Phoenix serviceAurora
questsQuest definitions, assignment, and completion trackingNode Lambdas behind API Gateway (separate stack, shared across titles)DynamoDB
live_opsEvent scheduling and seasonal contentin-process Quantum cron in this servicereward tables authored in Google Sheets and imported on a schedule

Client feature flags and ad kill-switches are not in this service at all - they live in Firebase Remote Config and are read by the Unity client. Live-event enable flags are a separate thing and are compile-time literals in this service's config (see Live-Ops Event Engine).

Endpoints & releasing

Phoenix serves the JSON game API plus a LiveView admin surface (player browser, dashboard, login) mounted under the browser pipeline. Routes are served unversioned under /api and health-checked at /health for the ALB. A representative controller and the release command:

elixir id}) do case Profile.get_player(id) do {:ok, player} -> json(conn, %{id: player.id, coins: player.coins, lives: player.lives}) {:error, :not_found} -> conn |> put_status(:not_found) |> json(%{error: "not_found"}) end end end # Build + run the release (baked into the Fargate image) # MIX_ENV=prod mix release zombies_game # _build/prod/rel/zombies_game/bin/zombies_game start]]>

Migrations do not run on boot. Run bin/zombies_game eval "ZombiesGame.Release.migrate()" as a one-off Fargate task before rolling the services, so a bad migration can't take down every task at once.

record.title: Domino Delights — Game Design Document
record.body:
Domino Delights (internal codename "Game of Dominoes" / GoD) is Harmony Games' tile-connecting puzzle title with light-RPG progression. This document is the living design reference for the core loop, character system, and retention mini-games. Store title is Domino Delights; use Game of Dominoes or GoD internally.

Built through the Baklava release train, which shipped 11 September 2024; the soft launch itself was the US go-live on 11 April 2025, worldwide on 6 May 2025. ~4,755 levels across 160 chapters are in production. This GDD supersedes the pre-soft-launch draft; see the version history for the edit trail.

Core Loop & Mechanics

Players match a face-up board tile against the tile in hand — tripeak-solitaire structure on domino tiles — drawing from the draw pile when nothing matches. Each unbroken match chain feeds a streak meter; sustained combos drive the light-RPG layer, where collected characters level up and unlock stronger board-clearing abilities. A single run alternates between board-clearing turns and character-ability triggers, keeping session length short but replayable across the ~4,755-level ladder.

Boosts

  • Magical Gust - a wind boost that clears all face-up tiles on the board, resetting a stalled position.
  • Character abilities (below) act as targeted boosts that recharge through matching.

For coin, life, and booster balancing that these mechanics feed into, see Economy Design - Coins, Lives & Boosters.

Characters

Four playable characters (Sophie is the starter, the other three are collectible), each with its own upgrade track. Leveling a character deepens its signature effect and reduces its recharge cost.

CharacterSignature abilityUpgrade track
SophieStarts unlocked. Adds tiles to the draw pile and turns tiles wildImproves draw quality and wild frequency
NathanRemoves a set of random face-up tiles; jumbo tile to handIncreases tiles removed per trigger and jumbo size
JuliusRemoves face-up tiles and converts them to gold or wildIncreases tiles converted per trigger
LexiForesight - reveals upcoming tilesExtends how far ahead she reveals

Wildcard is a booster (1,600 coins), not a character.

Character names and the fifth slot are provisional. Do not surface upgrade numbers in marketing until the economy pass locks recharge costs.

Retention Mini-Games

Between level runs, players can enter reward mini-games that keep engagement high on off-days:

  • Tile Dozer - a coin-pusher where dropped tiles shove a stacked tray toward the edge for coin and booster payouts.
  • Lucky Drop - a drop-and-bounce board awarding tiered rewards by landing slot (prototyped as "Plinko"; renamed for trademark reasons before ship).
  • River Tile - a timed matching mini-game (prototyped as "Conveyor Belt").
  • Memory Game - a pairs game on a timer.

Reward scaling for Tile Dozer and the other mini-games is tuned to daily-return targets and shares the coin sink with the core economy.

Competitive Context

Positioning benchmarks against the tile-matching leader are tracked in Competitive Analysis - Match Factory.

record.title: Zombie Match 3D — Game Design Document
record.body:
This is the living Game Design Document for Zombie Match 3D (shipped on the store as Puzzles vs Zombies under Calm Play LLC until the transfer to Harmony Games and the rename on 24 July 2025). It is the source of truth for the core loop, the RPG combat layer, and monetization. For the coin/life economy see Economy Design - Coins, Lives & Boosters, and for the paid track see ZM3D Season Pass - Spec. This document ladders up to Product OKRs - 2025 H1.

ZM3D never had a global launch. It first became publicly downloadable in the US on Google Play on April 12, 2025 and on the App Store on April 18, 2025; May 15, 2025 is the day iOS build 1.0.5 went live. This GDD reflects that build plus the Season Pass update.

Core mechanic

The matcher is a Match-3D collector benchmarked on Match Factory. Objects sit in a physics pile; the player drags items into a 7-slot tray. Collect any 3 matching objects and they clear from the tray. If all 7 slots fill without a match it counts as a blunder: the tray clears and surviving monsters enrage, but play continues. It is a tempo penalty, not a fail state - the loss screen only appears at zero health. Tray pressure is the primary difficulty dial.

  • Pile physics - objects settle and occlude each other; digging exposes buried matches.
  • 7-slot tray - the primary tempo penalty, not the fail state; tuning slot count changes felt difficulty more than object count.
  • Object families - cosmetic skins that map to elemental ammo in the RPG layer.

Zombie RPG layer

Levels wrap the matcher in combat. Each cleared triple fires the matching element at the current monster. Monsters carry an elemental weakness; hitting the weakness deals bonus damage and can apply a status.

Monster / element table

The roster is an everyday-people theme rather than classic undead. Minion families scale in tiers; bosses come in standard, Fast and Turbo variants.

Elemental weaknesses used by boosters and abilities: shock, poison, burn, freeze, splash, stun, blind. Glue is a booster, not an element.

Modes

  • Campaign - authored levels, escalating monster mixes.
  • Endless - survival board with an item refill every 30s to keep the pile stocked.
  • Infinite-HP Boss - a damage-race against a boss whose HP does not deplete to zero; the score is total damage dealt before the tray fills.

Monetization

The headline product is the Season Pass at $6.99, reached production in the week of September 22-29, 2025. It runs a free and a premium reward track over a fixed season window; progression is earned through campaign and Endless play. Coin, life, and booster sinks live in the linked Economy doc - do not duplicate values here.

Known launch issues (tracked, historical):

  • Hard crash from consecutive glass-impact SFX/VFX on Android, mostly Samsung (Aug-Sep 2025, ZOM-475), fixed by removing the glass SFX and VFX. The separate addressables splash-hang belongs to Domino Delights.
  • The font-download freeze that stalls the splash screen at ~22% on slow connections is also Domino Delights (ENG-2346, May 2025); the ZM3D client has no remote font download.

record.title: Combo Fighter — Game Design Document
record.body:
Combo Fighter is a merge / auto-battler prototype: the player drags shaped pieces onto a board — a Tetris family (I, L, S, T, square) plus a non-Tetris Lightning piece — merges matching pieces to upgrade them, connects them into combos, and then watches an auto-battle phase resolve the round. It was the last new concept Harmony Games took to a testable build — a skeleton crew put a playable MVP together in roughly four to five weeks, with the first TestFlight build on December 17, 2025 and the store listing live the following day, then the measured 1.0.62 / 1.0.72 / 1.0.88 builds. Those three measured builds account for 401 of Combo Fighter’s 901 lifetime installs; the other 500 landed before 1.0.62, from the first external installs on December 27, 2025 onward, and were reported to the board as a single figure. Of the three prototypes we shipped to store test tracks it posted the strongest early engagement, but it remains parked: we put a small Meta UA test behind it (low four figures) to see whether that engagement holds at scale. In-game ads are outside MVP scope.

Core Mechanics

A round has two distinct phases. The build phase is board manipulation; the battle phase is hands-off resolution.

Build phase

  • Drag & place. The tray offers Tetris-shaped pieces (I, L, S, T, square). The player drags a piece onto the board; it snaps to the grid.
  • Merge to upgrade. Two same-tier pieces of the same type that touch merge into the next tier — the familiar merge-2 loop, but on shaped pieces rather than single cells.
  • Connect for combos. Pieces wired into a contiguous chain form a combo; longer chains grant a battle-phase multiplier, so board layout drives power.

Battle phase

  • The assembled board becomes the player's squad and auto-battles the level's wave. No input during battle — the round is won or lost on how the board was built.
  • Rewards span several currencies. Silver is the in-round currency: selling a piece returns Silver, and Silver pays for re-rolls and for clearing frozen tiles. Gold pays for permanent Health, Damage and Regen upgrades and for unlocking special combos.

Ads: None in MVP. The MVP design has no interstitials or rewarded placements; ad SDK work began in the repo on 8 January 2026, after the MVP was scoped. Monetization was deliberately deferred until the core loop proved it retained, so the MVP measured engagement and retention.

Art direction

Simple Chibi-style 3D characters on a clean board. The look was chosen to be cheap to produce at prototype scale while still reading as a finished game in a store screenshot.

Scope — MVP

The build track was a 35-level MVP. The MVP existed to answer one question — does the merge-plus-auto-battle loop hold a player past the first session — before committing to the remaining content and the deeper progression curve.

  • Shipped in MVP: 35 levels, drag/merge/connect build loop, auto-battle resolution, gold economy, Chibi 3D art.
  • Built after the MVP: the level set grew from the 35-level MVP to 442 playable levels, the shipped count since 20 January 2026. The level file holds 485 entries in all: those 442 plus 14 daily puzzles and 29 test levels. Still open: meta-progression between runs, monetization surface, live-ops events.

Builds & Early Retention

TestFlight opened in mid-December 2025 and the first paid-UA installs landed on 27 December 2025; the second invite wave and builds 1.0.46-1.0.50 followed on January 6, 2026. The three measured builds are 1.0.62 (Jan 22), 1.0.72 (Jan 26) and 1.0.88 (Feb 4). D1 retention climbed with each later build even as install volume swung with test-track promotion.

BuildRelease dateInstallsD1 retention
1.0.62Jan 22, 202612725%
1.0.72Jan 26, 202624431%
1.0.88Feb 4, 20263043%

Session length was the standout signal: measured D0 averages — total play time per player on install day, summed across all of that player's sessions, not the length of a single session — were 48.74 minutes for build 1.0.62, 42.98 for 1.0.72 and 31.62 for 1.0.88, roughly 2.5x the ~20 minutes a player spends in the other two titles, because Combo Fighter is the only one of the three with no lives gate. By 1.0.88 the loop was tightening and D1 had reached 43% on a small install base, but we have not yet validated that at scale on a larger install base.

Related Pages

record.title: Economy Design — Coins, Lives & Boosters
record.body:
This page is the cross-game reference for how our soft and hard currencies, lives, and boosters are priced and tuned. It is owned by Design and kept in sync with the individual game design docs - see Domino Delights - Game Design Document and Zombie Match 3D - Game Design Document for the per-game economy layers built on top of these primitives.

Currency model

The currency model is per title. Zombie Match 3D uses coins, gems and bones; Domino Delights uses coins, gems and hero shards; Combo Fighter uses Silver, Gold, Experience, Gems and Tickets. Gems is the only currency common to all three by name; Combo Fighter's soft currencies are Silver and Gold rather than coins, so the shared primitive is the soft/hard pair, not the word "coins". Coins are the soft currency earned in play; gems are the premium hard currency bought or awarded sparingly. The conversion below is the Zombie Match 3D reference; Domino Delights adjusted its IAP payouts the same month (commit ceb6021fb, 9 April 2025):

UnitEqualsNotes

Level victories pay out coins on a per-level band, which anchors the earn side of the loop against the booster sinks below.

Zombie Match 3D item catalog

The ZM3D Master Item List is the source of truth for tunable objects: it currently holds 250 items spread across 21 categories (boosters, tiles, cosmetics, packs, and event-only entitlements). When adding a category, register it here first so the balancing sheet and the client stay aligned.

Booster costs

Currency units and values are title-specific; only the general soft-/hard-currency pattern is shared. The retained source confirms these Zombie Match 3D per-unit coin values and does not support a 1,500-coin, 30-minute unlimited assignment.

  • Domino Delights' main shop prices in coins on a much wider ladder; see Domino Delights - Game Design Document for the per-level earn curve these sit against.
  • The daily rotating shop carries gem-priced equivalents of the same boosters — Rewind 50, Dynamite 100, Draw 3 120, Wildcard 160, Gust 200 Gems — so the shop is not coin-only even though every in-level charge above is. Draw 5 has no shop SKU at all; 1,800 Coins is strictly the out-of-moves continue price.
  • The two games do not share a booster price band - only the currency model is shared.

The Domino Delights coin cut (April 2025)

In April 2025 we cut Domino Delights first-time level-completion coin rewards by 34.4% - the nine-cell star table fell from a 480-coin sum to 315 - to stop runaway coin inflation. A straight 50% cut was the preferred option on paper, but it is not what shipped. The star table was not the only faucet cut in the same window — on-board chest coins went 300 to 100, hourly collection 150 to 100, chapter rewards 1000 to 500, the 4-streak multiplier 80x to 40x, mini-game refresh 2h to 24h, and Lucky Drop's infinite-lives grant 1800s to 300s — which is why the p99 falls further than the star-table percentage alone would suggest. The 99th-percentile daily earn fell from about 25,000 coins to about 8,500. IAP payouts were re-tuned the same month (commit ceb6021fb, 9 April 2025); the size of that offset was never written down, so do not quote one. Do not revert reward payouts on GoD without re-running the sink analysis - the pre-cut curve is recoverable from commit 1ee438b6a6 and from the v2.0 economy workbook.

The symptom was that high-engagement players accumulated coins faster than any sink could absorb, so boosters felt free and the difficulty curve flattened. After the cut, average booster spend nudged up as expected and the coin balance distribution stopped climbing. The changes were applied to the live economy tables under the "Game of Dominoes" (GoD) codename and mirrored into this page's tuning constants.

Lives regeneration and refill pricing are game-specific and documented in each GDD. This page only fixes the shared currency and booster primitives.

record.body:
Owner: Frederick Stone (Growth/UA, departed Oct 2025). Scope: H1 2025 product objectives for Zombie Match 3D (shipped on the store as Puzzles vs Zombies until the July 2025 rename), scored against the metrics bar our investors expect to see before writing a Series A. This is the working scorecard we reviewed at the mid-year checkpoint.

Framing note: these OKRs were deliberately set to the VC bar for a hybrid-casual title - the numbers a growth investor needs to see (D1 north of 30%, CPI under $5, early ROAS trending toward payback). Hitting internal comfort levels is not the same as clearing a fundable bar. These are the retention and payback bars the team tracks against each half.

Objectives & Key Results

ZM3D never launched globally. It first became publicly downloadable in the US on Google Play on April 12, 2025 and on the App Store on April 18, 2025, shipped under the CalmPlay shell as Puzzles vs Zombies and renamed in July 2025, and it stayed on a short country list for the rest of its life. May 15, 2025 is the day iOS build 1.0.5 went live and paid UA resumed. Everything below is measured on the four weeks after that build unless noted. D30 ROAS is necessarily a projection at this point - the window closes before the launch-day cohort reaches D30, so it is modelled from early payback, not realised.

Objective / Key ResultTargetActualStatus
Launch ZM3D globallyMay 15, 2025Not shipped - US-only from April 2025 and still a short country list in September 2025; no localisation✗ Missed
D1 retention> 30%27.9% on the 408-install Aug-2025 UK iOS cohort (daily cohorts 22.9%-36.1%); the May-June 2025 builds read in the mid-20s✗ Missed
Blended CPI< $5.00Not measurable — the Unity→Singular cost connector reported $0 for the whole window while still delivering the bulk of the installs, so any blended figure computed from the surviving rows would divide a partial spend by the full install count and mean nothing— No data
D30 ROAS> 0.50.31 (projected)✗ Missed

Acquisition-channel split

Network labels must be scoped to the same window as the metric. In the retained trailing-four-week slice, paid-acquisition rows contain AppLovin and Unity Ads. Adjoe is documented separately for an earlier Domino Delights campaign. The retained slice does not support a Facebook-only claim or adding Google UAC.

Retro & conclusion

Candid retro: we missed even the one lever we control tactically - the global ship date never happened - and missed the ones that decide fundability (retention and ROAS). A sub-30% D1 with a projected D30 ROAS of 0.31 is a title that does not pay itself back in the window an investor underwrites. The best single daily cohort touched 36.1%, which tells us the ceiling is close - but a one-week peak is not a durable cohort, and we could not hold it once paid Facebook volume was in the blend.

Net: the ZM3D H1 metrics did not clear the bar a growth round is priced on. That result is what drove the decision to pursue a bridge round rather than a priced Series A - buy time to fix Facebook-cohort retention and pull D30 ROAS toward 0.5, then re-approach on stronger numbers. Design context and the intended retention loops live in Zombie Match 3D - Game Design Document.

H2 follow-ups

  • Rework the FTUE for Facebook-sourced installs; the day-two cliff is where the blend breaks.
  • Instrument per-channel D7/D30 ROAS separately (in Singular) so we stop hiding a bad cohort inside a passable blend.
  • Re-baseline the D1 > 30% OKR as a per-channel target, not a blended one.

record.title: Competitive Analysis — Match Factory
record.body:
Working notes from the Jan 7, 2025 Prototype Discussion. We are deciding whether to keep iterating on Domino Delights (internal codename "Game of Dominoes" / GoD) or pivot the next title to a 3D physics-matcher. The reference the room kept returning to is Match Factory, the current gold standard for 3D matching. This page lays out why its core loop out-retains the domino approach, and how Zombie Match 3D adapts the mechanic without cloning it.

Comparisons to Match Factory and Domino Dreams are based on public store listings and hands-on play only. We have no first-party numbers for either; treat all competitor reads as directional.

Why Match Factory wins on retention

The Match Factory loop is deceptively simple: tap identical objects from a physics pile, and any three of a kind clear. The tension lives entirely in the 7-slot tray at the bottom. If all seven slots fill without completing a triplet, you lose the board. That one constraint does a lot of work:

  • Legible failure state. Players know exactly why they lost - the tray filled - so a retry feels earned.
  • Short sessions. A board resolves in under a minute, which suits commute play and drives strong D1.
  • Readable difficulty. Tune tension via pile variety against the fixed 7-slot capacity.

Our Domino Delights (see Domino Delights - Game Design Document) never produced that pressure. Domino placement is open-ended, so there is no always-visible fail meter; sessions run long and the loss condition reads as fuzzy. Domino Dreams shows the same ceiling - pleasant, but softer hooks than the tray-based matchers.

Head-to-head

DimensionMatch Factory (3D matcher)Domino Delights / Domino Dreams
Core actionMatch 3 objects from a physics pilePlace and chain dominoes
Fail conditionFill the 7-slot tray, no tripletRun out of moves / soft block
Session lengthUnder a minute per boardMulti-minute, open-ended
Early retention readStrong D1, clean retry loopSofter hooks, fuzzier loss

How Zombie Match 3D differentiates

Cloning the loop is not the plan. Zombie Match 3D keeps the proven 7-slot tray as its puzzle skeleton, then stacks a zombie-combat RPG layer on top so matching drives more than clearing a board. Completed triplets resolve as attacks against a wave of zombies, turning each cleared set into combat output.

  • Puzzle skeleton (borrowed). Same physics pile and 7-slot tray players already understand from titles like Match Factory - but not its fail rule: in Zombie Match 3D a full tray is a blunder that clears the tray and enrages surviving monsters, and the level is lost only at zero health.
  • Combat layer (ours). Object types map to attack effects; the tray becomes a resource, not a pure meter.
  • RPG progression (ours). Upgrades and run structure give us a long-tail retention and monetization story the flat matcher category lacks.

Full mechanics and economy live in Zombie Match 3D - Game Design Document. The bet: inherit the matcher's clean, high-retention core and differentiate on combat/RPG, rather than competing head-on with an established pure-matcher.

Open question for the team: is the 7-slot constraint defensible design language rather than a copy? Consensus in the room was that pairing it with zombie combat clears that bar. - Robert

record.title: ZM3D Season Pass — Spec
record.body:
This is the product spec for the Zombie Match 3D Season Pass (shipped on the store as Puzzles vs Zombies under Calm Play LLC until the transfer to Harmony Games and the rename on 24 July 2025), written just before launch. The pass is the first paid track on the title and the primary lever we have for lifting ARPU on our existing daily actives. For the core loop, combat layer, and monetization overview this ladders under, see Zombie Match 3D - Game Design Document, and for the target it serves see Product OKRs - 2025 H1.

At a glance. Reached production in the week of September 22-29, 2025 - Android 0.3.127 published Sep 22, iOS 0.3.49 released Sep 29 at $6.99 (one-time unlock per monthly season). A free track and a premium track run in parallel over the monthly season window, with rewards unlocked by the same live-ops progression players already earn through play.

Goal & positioning

We monetize almost entirely through consumables (coins, boosters, extra lives). That caps ARPU because it only reaches players already willing to spend on a fail state. The Season Pass adds a low-friction, predictable monthly product that converts engagement - not frustration - into revenue, and gives non-payers a visible reason to log in daily via the free track.

  • Cadence - production seasons reset monthly on the 1st at 00:00 UTC; the initial launch may be a partial first season.
  • Earn, don't grind - pass points come from campaign clears, Endless runs, and daily quests. No separate currency to buy.
  • Level-gated, then always on - the pass unlocks at player level 30 by default and the unlock level is an active A/B variable. Once unlocked every player earns from tier 1; the premium track retro-unlocks all already-earned premium rewards at purchase.
  • One pass SKU - the monthly Season Pass at $6.99. There is no separate Battle Pass.

Reward tracks

Each season runs 30 tiers. The free track is deliberately front-loaded so the value of the premium track is legible before a player commits. Premium includes cosmetics and coin/gem sinks plus material advantages - notably raising life capacity from 5 to 8 - alongside booster bundles and gems.

Tier bandFree trackPremium track ($6.99)
1-5Coins, 1 boosterSeason avatar frame + coins
6-10Extra livesExclusive monster skin
11-20CoinsBooster bundles + gems
21-291 boosterCoins, gems, tray cosmetic
30Coin lump sumSignature seasonal skin + gem grant

Points model

Rollout

Ship to 100% on launch day rather than a slow ramp - the pass is time-boxed to a calendar month, so a partial rollout would leave early cohorts on a shortened first season. We gate on store approval and a live-ops config freeze the day before.

Rollout guardrails:

  • Do not touch tray count or Endless refill cadence during an active season - it swings the difficulty curve and skews pass-progression pacing right when we're reading purchase intent.
  • Season config (tiers, rewards, theme) is authored in the live-ops tool and locked 24h before each season opens; no hotfixes to reward tables mid-season without Product sign-off.
  • Purchase and tier-claim events are tagged for reporting through our attribution and analytics stack. There is no daily-active read on Zombie Match 3D - the title has no DAU table - so derive volume from installs and retention instead.

No Season Pass purchase has been recorded: the title's only store-validated sale is a $1.99 bundle on 31 July 2025. Treat season pacing as a design input rather than a revenue lever on this title. Owner: Robert (Product). Design partner: Julia Lawson. Both stayed through the February 2026 wind-down.

record.title: Harmony Games — Company Story & Mission
record.body:
Welcome to Harmony Games, Inc. (harmonygames.co). This is the studio overview for new hires — who we are, what we're building, and how we work. Read it first, then jump to the space for your discipline.

Who we are

Harmony Games is a small, remote-first mobile-game studio, founded in March 2023 and incorporated the following month in Delaware. We build hybrid-casual puzzle games — titles with the instant approachability of a casual game and the retention hooks of a light RPG. The team is distributed across three continents and runs lean by design (around sixteen non-founders at its peak, nineteen people including the three founders), keeping everyone close to the product.

The founding thesis comes from a specific background: 10+ years in gaming marketing plus a psychology degree. That pairing is the whole company in one sentence — we sit on the seam between marketing and product, and build games where the acquisition funnel and the core loop are designed together rather than handed off.

Mission

“A game of dominoes is really just match-3 in disguise — the same metrics, the same funnel. The opportunity is to take that casual approachability and deepen it: collection mechanics and a light RPG economy that give a player a reason to come back on day 30. Bridge marketing and product, and you get a game that is both cheap to acquire for and worth staying in.”

What we're building

Our titles, in the order the studio's focus moved to each:

WhenTitleDetail
Mar–Apr 2023Founded & incorporatedHarmony Games, Inc. founded March 2023; Delaware incorporation April 2023.
2023–2024Domino DelightsFirst title (internal codename "Game of Dominoes" / GoD) — tile-match with collection meta; benchmarked against Domino Dreams.
Jan 2025Zombie Match 3DStudio focus shifts to the match-3D RPG (store name "Puzzles vs Zombies"), benchmarked against Match Factory.
2025Combo Fighter (prototype)A third concept taken to prototype to test whether the hybrid-casual formula generalises beyond tile-match.

How we measure success

We measure product ambition against a fundability bar — the retention, CPI, and ROAS a growth round is underwritten on. That scorecard lives in Product OKRs — 2025 H1. Attribution across every title is standardised on Singular.

Where we are today: we've hit our tactical targets (ship dates, CPI), but day-30 retention and payback haven't yet cleared the bar a growth round is priced on. After the October 2025 cost reductions the studio ran on a skeleton crew - paid headcount fell from 13 to 8 - while the founders pursued a bridge or a strategic outcome to fund the next iteration. The 13 is the October payroll count and is inflated by partial-month termination payments (terminations went through Deel on 10/24), so it is not a month-end headcount. The near-term focus is proving day-30 retention holds — in hybrid-casual, the marketing-and-product seam only pays off if players stay past day one.

record.title: Release Checklist & Store Submission
record.body:
Owner: Vincent Parker (QA, departed Nov 2025) · Space: OPS. This is the gate every Harmony Games title passes before we submit a build to the App Store or Google Play. It applies to Zombie Match 3D (listed as "Puzzles vs Zombies" until the July 2025 rename), Domino Delights (internal codename GoD, "Game of Dominoes") and Combo Fighter. Do not submit a build until every box below is ticked and QA has signed off - the checklist exists because every item on it maps to a real incident that shipped.

Always test the UPDATE path from the last two shipped versions (N-1 and N-2), not just a fresh install. The June 2025 Domino Delights progression losses were never reproduced and no cause was established; the leading hypothesis was the update path. A fresh-install-only pass does not clear this gate.

Pre-submission checklist

Build & QA

  • Full manual regression is green on real iOS and Android hardware - see the QA Regression Runbook. QA sign-off is a hard gate.
  • Update path verified from N-1 and N-2: level, coins and unlocks survive the update; no save/progression loss.
  • Splash and loading screen watched all the way to gameplay on a throttled connection and with the app cache cleared - no stall (see incidents below).
  • Live quest config, if touched, has passed QA and a canary - nothing pushed straight to the live quest server (see the Quest System - Design & Incident Postmortem).

Store metadata & compliance

  • Version and build number bumped; release notes drafted for both stores.
  • Screenshots, age rating and data-safety / privacy declarations current.
  • IAP products and prices active in App Store Connect and Play Console before submission.
  • Analytics build tagged so installs attribute correctly (Singular).

Domino Delights is in maintenance mode - the current build is tracked under ENG-2366 (Jul 2025): IAP catalog refresh, difficulty tuning, interstitials disabled, and the negative-lives clamp. Run the same update-path and store checks against it; maintenance does not mean unreviewed.

Lessons from incidents

Each row is a bug that reached players. Treat the corresponding checklist item as non-negotiable.

TicketTitle / dateWhat happenedChecklist item it hardened
ENG-2346Domino Delights, May 2025 global-launch hot fixRemote font/asset download made the game look frozen at ~22% on the splash screen. Fixed by changing when fonts load and adding a downloading indicator.Watch splash to gameplay on a slow connection with cache cleared.
ENG-2343Domino Delights, May 2025 global-launch hot fixSplash / loading screen resolution was too low for new players; fixed by using higher-quality art.Verify splash and loading render correctly across device resolutions.
- Progression wipe, June 2025Player progression wiped for real players in production; never reproduced in-house and no cause established. The update path is the leading hypothesis, which is why this gate tests it - a fresh-install-only pass does not clear it.Test update from N-1 and N-2; confirm save/progression integrity.
ENG-2366Domino Delights maintenance, Jul 2025Maintenance build: IAP payout amounts refreshed (store SKUs and prices unchanged), difficulty tuning, interstitials disabled, negative-lives clamp (not a regeneration fix; the later ENG-2400 issue remained separate).Run full store + update checks even on maintenance-mode builds.

When any check fails, block the release, file the bug with device / OS / source build, and do not ship until it is green.

Notes on individual events

  • Nathan's Treasure Hunt - our best-performing GoD seasonal to date; the reward-ladder structure is the template we now reuse for one-off events.
  • Plague Race - the recurring ranked competition on ZM3D. In Aug 2025 the algorithmically generated levels - everything above level 100 - did not count toward the race, so high-level players could not score (ZOM-459, opened 5 Aug, fixed 25 Aug 2025). It affected scoring for players above level 100, so pre-fix placements and reward settlement in those races are unreliable — at least one player who was leading lost and had to be compensated by hand. It did not affect revenue; Plague Race carries no IAP.
  • Endless Monster Mode - a permanent ZM3D board mode, not a seasonal event. It unlocks at level 24 and resets daily at 00:00 UTC and weekly on Monday 00:00 UTC, both cron-scheduled in the CDK stack. ZOM-297 was closed on 1 Aug 2025, but that is the ticket close, not the ship: the mode reached players in the release submitted 6 Aug — Android 0.3.99 on 6 Aug, iOS 0.3.11 on 7 Aug 2025.

2025 weekend live-ops outage. Domino Delights' weekend events failed to activate, so the published calendar diverged from what players actually saw. QA first reported it on Sunday 29 June 2025 and the events were enabled by hand in the database that day; it recurred unfixed and was reported again on Saturday 12 July. The cause was a scheduler bug — the generator runs Sunday 00:00 UTC and set the Saturday–Sunday block to end on that same Sunday, six days before its own start, so the block never activated. Streak Fever was affected from 1 April and Axe Arena from 15 May. A one-line fix was committed on 19 July 2025. The record contains no deployment of that fix and no message confirming the calendar was healthy again, so this outage has no recorded end — do not quote a duration. The lives/energy problem reported in the same thread is a SEPARATE, client-side issue with its own open tickets; it is not part of this outage. Do not backfill or reason about that window from this calendar - the Live-Ops Event Engine page holds the reconstructed timeline and the revenue impact.

Planning cadence

As of January 2026, the studio had 7 people (4 paid non-founders and 3 founders), down from a September 2024 peak of 19 - so live-ops planning is deliberately lightweight - one recurring meeting and one shared calendar, not a dedicated ops team. The working rhythm:

  • Daily live-ops pod review. Design, led by Julia Lawson, walks the coming weeks; Frederick Stone participated before his October 2025 departure: which recurring slots fire and whether a one-off drops on top. Company-wide sync is the Friday all-hands.
  • There is no technical content lock. Reward tables are re-imported from Google Sheets hourly in production (IMPORT_REWARDS_SCHEDULE defaults to 0 * * * *), so a mid-window sheet edit reaches players within the hour. The 24h season-pass freeze in the Season Pass spec is a process control on top of that, not a mechanism. Windows are cron expressions in the CDK stack and do need a deploy to change.
  • Overlapping events are normal. Domino Delights runs four weekly events concurrently in production, and Zombie Match 3D overlaps Plague Race, Leagues and both Endless Monster resets. Avoiding overlap has been discussed as an aspiration but is not an operating rule.
  • Post-event read. Each event gets a short retro against its target from Product OKRs before the slot is reused.

The recurring slots (Endless Monster Mode (a permanent board mode with daily and weekly resets, not a seasonal event); Plague Race ranked) are the backbone of the calendar. One-off seasonals like Nathan's Treasure Hunt are layered on for spikes - they are the exception, not the base cadence, and should never displace a recurring slot without documented Product approval.

record.title: Customer Support Playbook
record.body:
First-line playbook for the four player-facing issues that drive the bulk of our inbound. It lets anyone covering the queue triage, reply, and escalate consistently. Scope is the live titles: Domino Delights (internal codename GoD, "Game of Dominoes") and Zombie Match 3D (listed as "Puzzles vs Zombies" until July 2025). When a symptom matches a known incident, say so plainly and give a real ETA rather than a canned apology.

Always capture platform + store version + device model and, where the player can find it, their in-game user id (Settings → About → tap the build number). Most escalations stall because the ticket is missing one of these.

Triage table

Match the reported symptom to the row, apply the resolution, and only escalate if the resolution does not clear it.

SymptomLikely causeFirst-line resolutionEscalate to
Lives not regenerating / timer stuckLives balance stuck, sometimes negative - a client-side regeneration/reconciliation bug, open since Apr 2025 (ENG-2277) and still recurring in Nov 2025 (ENG-2400). Cause never established, and it is NOT the Jul 2025 event-scheduler stallCapture platform, build and user id; ask backend to grant a manual lives top-up, which is how every reported case was actually cleared. Do not promise that regeneration resumes on its own - no fix was ever shippedBackend (manual lives grant); client team for the underlying bug
Lost progression / account back at level 1Guest accounts are keyed by a UUID + secret in local PlayerPrefs, so an uninstall destroys the only credentialIf they previously signed in with Apple or Google, ask them to sign in again. If not, the progress cannot be recovered (see below)Backend, only if the old player id can be found - a manual data transfer has been offered in this situation; there is no self-serve re-link tooling
Quests not appearing / empty slotsNov 2024 quest outage (ENG-1892) - an Ads-subtype quest row reached the live catalog and shipped clients could not deserialize the response, so the whole tray came back empty. Fixed 18 Nov 2024, so a report today is a different bugForce a session refresh; if slots stay empty, collect user id + timestamp and flagDesign + Backend (quests)
Frozen on splash at ~22%May 2025 font/asset download stallAsk them to switch networks (Wi-Fi ↔ cellular), clear app cache, and reinstall; confirm it reaches gameplayClient / QA

Lost progression on reinstall

A guest account lives entirely in local PlayerPrefs - a UUID plus a secret - so uninstalling the app destroys the only credential pointing at that save. In the June 2025 reports the player id was unchanged and only the progression was lost; the cause was never established and no ticket was cut. If the account was never linked, say plainly that the progress cannot be recovered - there is no email on file, no stored receipt and no re-link tooling.

  • Ask whether they ever signed in with Apple or Google from the settings screen.
  • Take the player ID that Helpshift attaches to the ticket and look them up in Metabase; confirm the level/coin balance matches their description.
  • If they never linked, tell them plainly that it cannot be recovered - do not promise a restore.

There is no merge or re-link step, so a grant lands on whatever account the player is holding now. Confirm in Metabase which account you are crediting before granting anything.

Canned responses

Personalise the greeting, keep the facts. Do not promise fixes we have not shipped.

  • Lives stuck: "We're aware of a bug that can stop lives regenerating correctly and our team has it open. I can't promise it will start filling again on its own, so I've added a lives top-up to your account now - if it happens again, just reply here and we'll top you up again."
  • Lost progress: "If you signed in with Apple or Google before, signing in again will bring your progress back. If you never signed in, I'm sorry - a reinstall clears the only credential tied to that save and we can't recover it.
  • Missing quests: "Quests should repopulate after a fresh session. If they're still empty, reply with your user id and when you noticed and I'll escalate."
  • Stuck at 22%: "That's a loading stall on our end. Please switch between Wi-Fi and mobile data, clear the app cache, and reinstall."

Known-issue notes arrive from QA before a build ships - see the QA Regression Runbook - and symptoms found during a submission are mirrored here via the Release Checklist & Store Submission.

Owner: Frederick Stone (Growth/UA, departed Oct 2025). This page maps the Metabase dashboards without conflating their backing systems. Product-analytics cards use title-specific Firebase-to-BigQuery marts. Server-event investigation uses the API Gateway/Kinesis/Firehose/S3 lake through Glue and Athena. Singular supplies attribution.

Each title has its own Firebase project and product boards; there is no single cross-title filter.

Standard dashboards

These are the dashboards we keep pinned and review on a regular cadence. They cover the full loop from acquisition through retention and monetization. Names are illustrative - the actual collection names in Metabase may differ slightly, but the purpose and audience below are what matters.

DashboardPurposeAudience
DAU & RetentionDaily active users, session length, and D1/D7/D30 retention curves by title and cohort.Whole studio; reviewed at the Friday all-hands.
FTUE FunnelFirst-time-user-experience completion - level start / complete / fail drop-off through the onboarding funnel.Product & game design.
UA / CPI / ROAS by ChannelUser acquisition performance - spend, installs, blended and per-channel CPI, and D7/D30 ROAS, joined from Singular attribution.Growth/UA (Frederick Stone until his October 2025 departure); exec on investor prep.
Monetization - IAP / ARPUIn-app-purchase revenue, ARPU / ARPPU, conversion, and Season Pass attach + completion.Product & finance.
Live-Event PerformanceParticipation, completion, and revenue lift per live event vs baseline days.Live-ops & product.

How to read them

  • Every card is date-partitioned; default range is the trailing 28 days. Widen the filter for launch-window cohort views.
  • UA numbers reconcile to Singular, not to store console - attribution windows differ, so expect small deltas.
  • Retention is measured on activity, not installs; a reinstall inside the window counts as a returning user, not a new one.

Metric definitions live with the OKRs

This page tells you which dashboard to open. It does not define what a metric means. D1 retention, blended CPI, D30 ROAS, ARPU - those definitions, and the targets we hold them to, are owned alongside the objectives in Product OKRs - 2025 H1. If a dashboard number and an OKR number disagree, the OKR definition wins and the Metabase card is the thing to fix.

Do not fork a dashboard to "redefine" a metric for one analysis. If you need a variant (e.g. per-channel D1 instead of blended), add a card to the existing collection so the definition stays traceable. Silent metric drift between a fork and the canonical card is how two people end up quoting different D1 numbers in the same meeting.

Titles currently instrumented into these dashboards: Zombie Match 3D (listed as Puzzles vs Zombies until the July 2025 rename), Domino Delights (codename GoD), and Combo Fighter. Each title has its own Firebase project (domino-delights, zombie-match-3d, combo-fighter) and therefore its own BigQuery export and its own boards - there is no single cross-title filter. Coverage is uneven: Domino Delights has a modelled DAU table, Zombie Match 3D never did (derive its volume from installs x retention), and Combo Fighter's dataset was still being wired into dbt in Dec 2025.
